intro: Repeated matrix multiplication amplifies dominant directions. Follow a specified number of normalized iterations and inspect the final Rayleigh quotient.
task: Return the final unit vector and its Rayleigh quotient after exactly the requested number of power-iteration steps.
requirements: matrix is square and symmetric within absolute tolerance 1e-10. start is a matching vector with norm above 1e-12. steps is an integer in [0,1000].
Normalize start, then repeat v=matrix@v followed by unit normalization exactly steps times. Return {"vector": v, "rayleigh": v.T@matrix@v}.
Reject any intermediate norm at or below 1e-12. Preserve the sign produced by the recurrence; convergence is not guaranteed for every starting vector.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: One step
No multiplication
Known eigenvector

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Normalize the starting direction even when no multiplication steps are requested.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: Each iteration uses the previous unit vector. Preserve the recurrence sign rather than applying a sign convention afterward.

explanation: Normalizing each iterate prevents magnitude growth from obscuring direction. With a separated dominant eigenvalue and a nonzero component in its eigenspace, the direction approaches that eigenspace.
The Rayleigh quotient reports the matrix action along the current unit vector. Zero steps is still meaningful: it evaluates the normalized starting direction without claiming convergence.
